intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Wolfram syndrome-2 (WFS2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CISD2 gene (611507) on chromosome 4q24.

paragraphs.text: Wolfram syndrome-2 (WFS2) is an autosomal recessive disorder. It was first described in consanguineous Jordanian families with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and optic atrophy. Unlike the classic form of Wolfram syndrome, these families had no diabetes insipidus, and several patients had profound upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding (El-Shanti et al., 2000). A later patient had optic neuropathy without optic atrophy, high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and a platelet aggregation defect (Mozzillo et al., 2014).

checks.claim: Wolfram syndrome-2 (WFS2) is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder for which only insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and optic atrophy are necessary to make the diagnosis
checks.explanation: The abstract describes Wolfram syndrome as autosomal recessive, but it does not use the name WFS2 for the 4q-linked form.

checks.claim: WFS2 was first described in consanguineous Jordanian families with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and optic atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: 16 patients from four different families were recruited. These patients, who have the Wolfram syndrome phenotype, also have additional features that have not previously been reported.
checks.explanation: The families and the IDDM/optic atrophy phenotype are described, but the abstract does not say the families were Jordanian or consanguineous. The full text may say so.

checks.claim: Unlike classic Wolfram syndrome, the Jordanian WFS2 families had no diabetes insipidus.
checks.evidence_quote: There is an absence of diabetes insipidus in all affected family members.
checks.explanation: The absence of diabetes insipidus is stated. The abstract does not identify the families as Jordanian, and the comparison with classic Wolfram syndrome is implied rather than stated.

checks.evidence_quote: In addition, several patients have profound upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding.
checks.explanation: The GI ulceration and bleeding are stated. The abstract does not identify the families as Jordanian.

paragraphs.text: Mozzillo et al. (2014) described a Caucasian Italian girl with WFS2 whose parents said they were not consanguineous. From age 5 years she had recurrent bleeding upper intestinal ulcers. At 14 years she was diagnosed with malrotation and partial duodenal intussusception, which needed resection. At 16 years she developed reduced visual acuity, dyschromatopsia and bilateral optic disc pallor. Nonautoimmune diabetes mellitus began at 17 years and was treated with insulin. She also had bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, slow intestinal transit and entero-gastric bile reflux.

paragraphs.text: Mozzillo et al. (2014) concluded that this patient had optic neuropathy rather than optic atrophy. Fundus examination showed slight bilateral optic disc pallor, and pupillary light reflexes were preserved. Pattern VEPs were normal, and brain MRI showed normal optic nerve caliber. Visual field testing, ERG, microperimetry and OCT showed moderate involvement of the optic nerve in both eyes. These findings were stable over 5 years of follow-up, and at age 22 years she had no optic atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Mozzillo et al. (2014) found that their WFS2 patient had a reduced, reversible platelet aggregation defect in response to ADP at concentrations up to 10 microM, and no platelet secretion in response to ADP. Aggregation in response to collagen, epinephrine and ristocetin was normal. Her bleeding score was 3 (normal 3 or less), and other coagulation tests were normal. Her heterozygous parents and brother also had a reversible platelet aggregation defect in response to ADP, but none of them had ophthalmologic abnormalities, diabetes or deafness. The authors noted that the Jordanian patients had been reported to have defective aggregation to collagen rather than to ADP.

paragraphs.text: Amr et al. (2007) studied 3 consanguineous families of Jordanian descent with Wolfram syndrome. These families had previously been shown not to carry WFS1 mutations and had been mapped to the WFS2 locus. In all 3 families, Amr et al. (2007) identified a homozygous mutation in the ZCD2 (CISD2) gene: a G-to-C transversion at nucleotide 109 (c.109G-C) predicting a glu37-to-gln (E37Q) substitution at a conserved residue. They concluded that the mutation causes disease by disrupting mRNA splicing, which eliminates exon 2 and introduces a premature stop codon.

paragraphs.text: In a Caucasian Italian girl with WFS2, Mozzillo et al. (2014) identified a novel homozygous intragenic deletion of the CISD2 gene that removed all of exon 2. They detected it because exon 2 failed to amplify by PCR, and they confirmed it by cDNA sequencing. SNP-array analysis of the trio limited the deletion to a maximum size of 2,050 bp, extending from intron 2 to intron 3, with a minimum size of 739 bp (GRCh38). Her parents and brother were heterozygous carriers. The authors noted that the deleted region includes the codons for amino acids WRSKT (residues 102 to 106) within the 2Fe-2S domain, which may result in a nonfunctional protein.

paragraphs.text: Chen et al. (2009) showed that Cisd2 is located mainly in the mitochondria. In Cisd2 knockout mice, mitochondrial degeneration appeared to directly trigger accelerated aging. The authors concluded that their findings support the earlier clinical hypothesis that Wolfram syndrome is partly a mitochondria-mediated disorder, and they proposed that CISD2 mutation causes WFS2 in humans as a mitochondria-mediated disorder.

The authors proposed the Cisd2 knockout mouse as an animal model of WFS2.

paragraphs.text: Amr et al. (2007) studied 3 consanguineous Jordanian families with WFS2 that had no WFS1 mutations and had been mapped to the WFS2 locus. In affected members of all 3 families, they identified a homozygous G-to-C transversion at nucleotide 109 (c.109G-C) of the ZCD2 (CISD2) gene, predicting a glu37-to-gln (E37Q) substitution at a conserved residue. They concluded that the mutation disrupts mRNA splicing, which eliminates exon 2 and introduces a premature stop codon. Lymphoblastoid cells from affected individuals showed a significantly greater rise in intracellular calcium than control cells after stimulation with thapsigargin.

checks.claim: Amr et al. (2007) studied 3 consanguineous Jordanian families with WFS2 that had no WFS1 mutations and had been mapped to the WFS2 locus.
checks.evidence_quote: It had been shown that these families did not have mutations in the WFS1 gene (WFS1) but were mapped to the WFS2 locus at 4q22-25.

checks.claim: In affected members of all 3 Jordanian WFS2 families, Amr et al. (2007) identified a homozygous c.109G-C transversion in the ZCD2 (CISD2) gene.
checks.evidence_quote: A single missense mutation was identified in a novel, highly conserved zinc-finger gene, ZCD2, in three consanguineous families of Jordanian descent
checks.explanation: The title says the mutation is homozygous, and the abstract places the G-->C change at nucleotide 109.

checks.claim: The CISD2 c.109G-C mutation predicts a glu37-to-gln (E37Q) substitution at a conserved residue.
checks.evidence_quote: A G-->C transversion at nucleotide 109 predicts an amino acid change from glutamic acid to glutamine (E37Q). Although the amino acid is conserved

checks.claim: Amr et al. (2007) concluded that the CISD2 c.109G-C mutation disrupts mRNA splicing, eliminating exon 2 and introducing a premature stop codon.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation was found to disrupt messenger RNA splicing by eliminating exon 2, and it results in the introduction of a premature stop codon.

checks.claim: Lymphoblastoid cells from individuals homozygous for CISD2 c.109G-C showed a significantly greater rise in intracellular calcium than control cells after thapsigargin stimulation (Amr et al., 2007).
checks.evidence_quote: Lymphoblastoid cells from affected individuals show a significantly greater rise in intracellular calcium when stimulated with thapsigargin, compared with controls
checks.explanation: The affected individuals are the ones who carry the homozygous mutation.

paragraphs.text: In a Caucasian Italian girl with WFS2, Mozzillo et al. (2014) identified a homozygous intragenic deletion of the CISD2 gene that removed all of exon 2. Exon 2 failed to amplify by PCR, and the deletion was confirmed by cDNA sequencing. SNP-array analysis of the trio placed the deletion between intron 2 and intron 3, with a maximum size of 2,050 bp and a minimum size of 739 bp (GRCh38). Her parents and brother were heterozygous carriers. The deleted region includes the codons for residues 102 to 106 (WRSKT) within the 2Fe-2S domain, which the authors suggested may result in a nonfunctional protein. The patient had optic neuropathy without optic atrophy, insulin-treated diabetes mellitus, high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, recurrent bleeding upper intestinal ulcers, and a platelet aggregation defect in response to ADP.

checks.claim: In a Caucasian Italian girl with WFS2, Mozzillo et al. (2014) identified a homozygous intragenic CISD2 deletion removing all of exon 2.
checks.evidence_quote: CISD2 cDNA sequencing revealed a novel homozygous deletion affecting the whole exon 2 of CISD2

checks.claim: CISD2 exon 2 failed to amplify by PCR in the Italian WFS2 girl, and the deletion was confirmed by cDNA sequencing (Mozzillo et al., 2014).
checks.evidence_quote: In the patient the amplification of CISD2 exon 2 was not detected, while exons 1 and 3 were regularly present.
checks.explanation: PCR failure plus cDNA sequencing showing the deletion.

checks.claim: SNP-array analysis of the trio placed the CISD2 exon 2 deletion between intron 2 and intron 3, with a maximum size of 2,050 bp and a minimum size of 739 bp (GRCh38).
checks.evidence_quote: The minimum size of deletion was 739 bp while the maximum size was 4,250 bp. Combining these data with the ones from PCR, we were able to map the proximal breakpoint
checks.explanation: Array-only maximum was 4,250 bp; the 2,050 bp intron 2 to intron 3 limit came from combining array with PCR data.

checks.claim: The parents and brother of the Italian WFS2 girl were heterozygous carriers of the CISD2 exon 2 deletion.
checks.evidence_quote: The deletion was homozygous in the proband and heterozygous in her parents and brother.

checks.claim: The region removed by the CISD2 exon 2 deletion includes the codons for residues 102 to 106 (WRSKT) within the 2Fe-2S domain.
checks.evidence_quote: the triplets coding for aminoacids WRSKT, from the position 102 to 106 of the polypeptide, are within the deleted region

checks.claim: Mozzillo et al. (2014) suggested that the CISD2 exon 2 deletion may result in a nonfunctional protein.
checks.evidence_quote: this may result in a non functional protein because of zinc-finger domain lost.

checks.claim: The Italian WFS2 girl homozygous for the CISD2 exon 2 deletion had optic neuropathy without optic atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Our patient does not show optic atrophy, one of the main diagnostic criteria for WFS, but optic neuropathy.

checks.claim: The Italian WFS2 girl homozygous for the CISD2 exon 2 deletion had insulin-treated diabetes mellitus.
checks.evidence_quote: At 17 years old non-autoimmune diabetes occurred and WFS2 was suspected. She started insulin treatment.

checks.claim: The Italian WFS2 girl homozygous for the CISD2 exon 2 deletion had high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss.
checks.evidence_quote: Further examinations showed a bilateral sensorineural hearing loss in the high frequencies (SHLHF)

checks.claim: The Italian WFS2 girl homozygous for the CISD2 exon 2 deletion had recurrent bleeding upper intestinal ulcers.
checks.evidence_quote: Since the age of 5 years old, FS suffered from recurrent b-UIU.

checks.claim: The Italian WFS2 girl homozygous for the CISD2 exon 2 deletion had a platelet aggregation defect in response to ADP.
checks.evidence_quote: Evaluating PA, a reduced and reversible defective PA up to 10 μM of ADP was present
